newsitem.title: POLAND: Bishops invoke conscience in Polish referendum.
newsitem.headline: Bishops invoke conscience in Polish referendum.

text.p: Poland's Roman Catholic Episcopate on Friday urged Catholics to vote according to their own conscience in a nationwide constitutional referendum on May 25.

"Polish bishops have appealed to the faithful to be guided by their own conscience and to decide in accordance with it whether to reject or support the constitution," PAP news agency reported the Episcopate's secretary general, Bishop Tadeusz Pieronek, as saying.

He made the statement after the Episcopate's latest conference which reiterated the Church's resolve to avoid telling Catholics how to vote on the draft constitution adopted by Poland's leftist-dominated parliament early last month.
But the bishop also said Episcopate members had noted some of the constitution's shortcomings, including inadequate protection of human life.

Senior churchmen have expressed misgivings over such questions as the constitution's failure to protect human life from the moment of conception and to declare the supremacy of "natural (divine) law" over man-made legislation.

The rightist pro-Catholic Solidarity Election Alliance (AWS) has created its own constitutional draft which reflects Church teaching and is strongly urging Poles to vote against the parliamentary draft in this month's referendum.
But by appealing to the conscience of voters the bishops have clearly distanced themselves from rightist parties in and outside of the AWS which are fiercely campaigning for a "no" vote.
Earlier, Bishop Pieronek rejected attempts to involve the Church in political games and have "God conduct politics in people's behalf."
He also said that the Church bore no responsibility for anti-constitutional leaflets distributed by political activists during Sunday mass or plastered on parish premises.
